name: Precision
summary: Standard smoothing for slow, fine aim. Higher is smoother but heavier.

where.text: Edit your Config (pencil icon). In Mouse Aim or Motion Aim, set Smoothing to Custom instead of a preset, and make sure the smoothing button reads STANDARD (press it to change modes). Precision is one of the Standard settings.

citations.quote: To edit the current Config, press the pencil icon.
Here you can set Sensitivity (remember that lower values are faster) and Smoothing.
Motion aim settings consists of Sensitivity and Smoothing.
You can also customize the smoothing system and choose between two smoothing modes: Standard and Classic.
It's recommended you use one of the smoothing presets. If you are using "custom", ensure you do not reduce smoothing intensity below that of the presets.
Press the the smoothing button (i.e. "STANDARD" or "CLASSIC") to change modes.
Precision Controls fine aim behavior

definition.text: Controls fine aim behavior. Higher values provide a smoother result at low aim speeds and increases the heaviness of the reticle.

citations.quote: Controls fine aim behavior
Higher values provide a smoother result at low aim speeds and increases the heaviness of the reticle.

plainWords.text: It acts on slow movements: the small corrections you make while lining up or holding on a target. Raising it smooths those movements more.

citations.quote: Controls fine aim behavior
Higher values provide a smoother result at low aim speeds and increases the heaviness of the reticle.

plainWords.text: Lowering it should do the opposite: small adjustments feel lighter but get less smoothing.

citations.quote: Higher values provide a smoother result at low aim speeds and increases the heaviness of the reticle.

plainWords.reasoning: The guide only describes raising it (smoother, heavier). Lowering it is the reverse of that stated trade-off.

plainWords.text: The guide doesn't give this setting's range or default. Check what Manager shows before you change it.

feel.text: Higher Precision makes the reticle feel heavier at low speed, in return for a smoother result.

citations.quote: Higher values provide a smoother result at low aim speeds and increases the heaviness of the reticle.

guidance.text: The guide gives no recommended value for this setting. It says smoothing is "strictly based on preference" and suggests trying the presets first.

citations.quote: Both mouse and motion have different presets designed for those aiming methods. Start by trying each out to see what feels most natural to you. It's strictly based on preference.

aimStyles.text: Tracking: the main lever. Raising Precision steadies your hold through sustained fire, at the cost of a heavier reticle. If small corrections feel sluggish, lower it.

citations.quote: Controls fine aim behavior
Higher values provide a smoother result at low aim speeds and increases the heaviness of the reticle.

aimStyles.reasoning: Tracking is mostly slow, fine movement, which is what Precision controls ("fine aim behavior", "smoother result at low aim speeds"). The heaviness trade-off comes from the same definition.

aimStyles.text: Precision hold: matters too. Lining up one careful shot is slow, fine movement. More Precision gives a steadier line-up but a heavier feel.

citations.quote: Controls fine aim behavior
Higher values provide a smoother result at low aim speeds and increases the heaviness of the reticle.

aimStyles.reasoning: Precision acts at low aim speeds, and a deliberate line-up happens at low speed.

aimStyles.text: Snap: matters less. A snap starts from rest, which Easing shapes, and the move itself is fast aim, which Response controls. Precision still shapes the small correction at the end of a snap.

citations.quote: Controls fine aim behavior
Controls fast aim behavior
Specifies aim behavior from rest

aimStyles.reasoning: Precision controls "fine aim behavior" and acts "at low aim speeds". A snap starts from rest (Easing "Specifies aim behavior from rest") and then moves fast (Response "Controls fast aim behavior"). The small correction at the end of a snap is slow, fine aim, which is where Precision acts.

confusions.name: Micro (Advanced SAB)
confusions.note: An Advanced SAB value that "Tunes stick behavior at very low aiming speeds". It belongs to Simulate Analog Behavior, not to smoothing.
